text.p: TCF Financial Corp, a $6.96 billion bank holding company, said Wednesday it backs a First Call consensus earnings estimate of $3.38 a share for the full year 1997.
"That's probably a pretty good bet, and that takes into consideration both the Standard and Winthrop pending acquisitions," said William Cooper, TCF chairman and chief executive officer.
"Without those acquisitions, ... it would be a 15 percent increase," Cooper told Reuters in an interview Wednesday before the company's annual meeting here.

On March 17, TCF agreed to acquire Standard Financial Inc, a Chicago-based thrift institution, for a combination of stock and cash. The merger is expected to close this autumn and will be accounted as a purchase transaction.

On February 28, TCF agreed to acquire in a tax-free stock swap Winthrop Resources Corp, a Minnesota-based company that leases business equipment. The acquisition is expected to close this summer and will be accounted as a pooling of interests.
Shares of TCF were up 1/4 to 39-7/8.
